te: Working group reports received: new fitness tests, new-recruit training and veterans' entitlements
se: The meeting received working group reports, such as on the Royal Thai Army's new physical fitness test, regulations and courses for new-recruit training, a framework for using reserve forces to help with disaster relief, veterans' current entitlements, and preparations for a forum on new forms of threat
it: Report of the armed forces structure working group: fitness tests and new-recruit training
Report of the reserve forces working group: using reserve forces to support disaster relief
Report of the veterans working group: veterans' benefits

te: 5 urgent tasks set for October 2024 to March 2025
se: The meeting followed up the work of 4 working groups and set 5 urgent tasks: following up the death of a conscript during training, studying applications from men liable for service to serve as conscripts by request (special case) online, preparing a physical fitness test manual, studying the use of reserve forces to support disaster relief, and studying veterans' benefits. It also prepared issues for discussion with the Minister of Defence and considered linking reserve force databases between agencies
it: 5 urgent tasks of the working groups
Linking the national reserve force database systems

te: First meeting: work divided into armed forces structure, reserve forces and veterans groups
se: The meeting noted the list of advisers to be proposed for approval, considered its duties and the overall picture of its work, and divided the work into groups: an armed forces structure group, which is urgently studying applications from men liable for service to serve as conscripts by request (special case) online and a physical fitness test manual for personnel; a reserve forces group, which is urgently studying the use of reserve forces to support disaster relief; and a veterans group
it: List of advisers to the subcommittee
Division of work into groups, and urgent tasks

te: Artificial intelligence and employment in Thailand: the Department of Employment and the Department of Skill Development invited to the meeting
se: Meeting on Thursday, 19 November 2026, at 13.00, Meeting Rooms 406–407, Floor 4, Parliament House. According to the meeting notice, the main item is to consider ways to address the impact of developments in artificial intelligence technology on employment in Thailand, with representatives of the Department of Employment and the Department of Skill Development invited to join the meeting, and to follow up the work of the subcommittees. The summary will be added after the Senate publishes it
it: Consideration of ways to address the impact of developments in artificial intelligence technology on employment in Thailand (representatives of the Department of Employment and the Department of Skill Development invited)
Progress of the subcommittees' work

te: Pre-meeting video · Draft maritime labour law: private sector bodies concerned invited to give information
Draft maritime labour law: report to be drafted, and a framework set for studying 2 more draft laws on labour courts
se: The meeting continued its study of the draft Maritime Labour Act (including views from the ILO Country Office for Thailand). The secretariat will draft a report for the meeting to adopt before it goes to the Senate. The meeting set a timeframe for studying the draft Act on the Establishment of Labour Courts and Labour Procedure (No. ..) and the draft Act on Procedure for Human Trafficking Cases (No. ..) under rule 119, inviting agencies such as the Office of the Council of State and the Office of the Judiciary to give information on 12 November 2026
it: Draft Maritime Labour Act (No. ..) B.E. ....: study report to be drafted for the meeting to adopt before it goes to the Senate
Timeframe for studying the draft Act on the Establishment of Labour Courts and Labour Procedure (No. ..) and the draft Act on Procedure for Human Trafficking Cases (No. ..)
Subcommittees: outline of a report on managing work for older people in the community economy ecosystem and food tourism · draft Homeworkers Protection Act (No. ..)

te: Meeting summary video · Draft maritime labour law: report to be drafted, and a framework set for studying 2 more draft laws on labour courts
Draft maritime labour law: seafarers' social security rights, and work by those under 18
se: The meeting continued its study of the draft Maritime Labour Act (No. ..). The Office of the Council of State explained 2 key points: extending social security and workmen's compensation coverage to seafarers (section 4) and adjusting the rules on work by seafarers under 18 years of age (section 16). The Department of Medical Services explained the role of the Ministry of Public Health, such as seafarers' health checks and medical certificates. The meeting also followed up the subcommittees' work; the Subcommittee on Social Security will meet on 11 November 2026 to discuss approaches to setting up a labour bank
it: Draft Maritime Labour Act: extending social security and workmen's compensation coverage to seafarers (section 4) · work by seafarers under 18 years of age (section 16)
Subcommittees: law on the employment of older persons · effects of government service contracts on social security rights · approaches to setting up a labour bank (meeting on 11 November 2026)

te: Meeting summary video · Draft maritime labour law: seafarers' social security rights, and work by those under 18
Draft maritime labour law: the Department of Labour Protection and Welfare and agencies concerned heard
se: The meeting studied the draft Maritime Labour Act (No. ..) B.E. ...., which the House of Representatives has accepted in principle at first reading, under rule 119 of the Senate Rules of Procedure, inviting the agencies concerned to give information, such as on the key amendment placing seafarers under the social security and workmen's compensation laws in line with the Maritime Labour Convention (MLC 2006), and followed up the subcommittees' work
it: Study of the draft Maritime Labour Act (No. ..) B.E. .... under rule 119 of the Senate Rules of Procedure
Following up the work of all 3 subcommittees (Employment Services and Skills Development · Labour Welfare and Protection · Social Security)

te: Meeting summary video · Draft maritime labour law: the Department of Labour Protection and Welfare and agencies concerned heard
Riders' safety and rights, and a plan to study the draft maritime labour law
se: The meeting invited the Department of Labour Protection and Welfare and the Electronic Transactions Development Agency to give information on protecting the benefits and safety of riders, planned its study of the draft Maritime Labour Act (No. ..) under rule 119, inviting 7 agencies including the International Labour Organization, prepared to present its report on a National Labour Development Digital Platform (NLDD) to the Senate on 19 October 2026, and followed up the subcommittees' work
it: Approaches to protecting the benefits and safety at work of riders (the Department of Labour Protection and Welfare and ETDA invited to give information)

te: Meeting summary video · Riders' safety and rights, and a plan to study the draft maritime labour law
Thai–Sri Lankan labour cooperation, and a proposal on employing persons with disabilities
se: The meeting invited agencies to give information on the memorandum of understanding and agreement between Thailand and Sri Lanka on employing Sri Lankan workers in Thailand. It considered a petition proposing a higher rate of employment of persons with disabilities under section 33 and bringing those working under section 35 into the social security system, agreeing to refer it to the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities and the Department of Labour Protection and Welfare to study its suitability, and prepared to present 2 reports to the Senate
it: Memorandum of understanding and agreement on labour between Thailand and the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka
Petition: raise the rate of employment of persons with disabilities under section 33 and bring employment under section 35 into the social security and labour protection systems
Subcommittees: preparations to present 2 reports to the Senate
